items.title: Live Updates: Scale of Flood Disaster Grows as Nepal Doubles Estimate of Missing
items.summary: A spokeswoman for the Nepali disaster relief agency said the tally grew to 1,900 after some 900 people were reported missing from hydropower projects. Rescue efforts were complicated by fears of new flooding.

items.title: Inside Afghanistan’s Secret Schools for Girls
items.summary: The Taliban have banned education for millions of Afghan girls. Times journalists examined classrooms where students, teachers and parents continue to resist by defying the rules.

items.title: Why Many Iranians Are Losing Hope After Six Months of War
items.summary: Iranians have become increasingly desperate, as they grapple with an economic crisis made worse by the conflict and grow increasingly skeptical about President Trump’s motives.

items.title: Fear Over Malaysia’s Plan to Send Back Rohingya Migrants to Myanmar
items.summary: The announcement has sent panic through a community that fled its country’s brutal military rule, civil war, religious persecution or some combination of the three.

items.title: Six Months In, Iran Appears Stronger and U.S. Goals Unclear
items.summary: Trump’s replacement of a military war with a heightened economic one is not expected to alter Iran’s strategy, while further impoverishing its people.

items.title: Disaster Experts Say Nepal Glacier Collapse Was Difficult to Predict
items.summary: Given the challenges in forecasting and detecting such calamities, researchers advised banning construction on floodplains and marking out clear evacuation routes.

items.title: Why Putin Is Fighting On, Even as His Problems Multiply
items.summary: There is little sign that public exhaustion, economic headwinds or increased Ukrainian strikes are changing the Russian leader’s view that he will eventually achieve victory.

items.title: Who Is Haakon, Norway’s New King?
items.summary: Crown Prince Haakon, the only son of King Harald V, will become monarch, a largely ceremonial and symbolic role.

items.title: ‘The Sauna Is Hot and Uncomfortable’: Vote on E.U. Talks Makes Iceland Sweat
items.summary: The usually genial country has been bitterly divided over a vote this weekend on whether to enter membership talks with the European Union.

items.title: You Can Photograph This Pretty Irish Castle. You Just Can’t Go In.
items.summary: Tourists still flock to the picturesque 16th-century Dunguaire Castle on Galway Bay. But in recent years, a dispute over ownership has prevented visitors from entering.

items.title: Chevron Is in Talks to Expand in Venezuela, a Potential Win for Trump
items.summary: President Trump’s administration has been pushing U.S. companies like Chevron to invest more in Venezuela’s oil industry.

items.title: Trump Updates $15 Billion Libel Lawsuit Against The New York Times
items.summary: The president has argued that the news organization sought to undermine his 2024 presidential campaign by disparaging his reputation as a businessman. The Times has moved to dismiss the lawsuit.

items.title: Investors Expect Higher Rates After Fed Chairman’s Inflation Pledge
items.summary: Kevin Warsh reiterated the Federal Reserve’s commitment to tackle rising prices, nudging up investor expectations of a rate increase.

items.title: China Sees Opportunity in America’s Recent A.I. Security Scares
items.summary: A leading Chinese A.I. start-up released its latest model and made the case that China’s embrace of open software is safer than Silicon Valley’s closed approach.

items.title: Smaller Revision Points to More Accurate Jobs Numbers
items.summary: The 2026 revisions by the Bureau of Labor Statistics represent a downward adjustment of just 0.1 percent of the total work force.

items.title: Companies Can Tell Investors Less Under Proposed S.E.C. Rules
items.summary: Fewer audit and disclosure requirements could reduce costs, but experts say they could also help disguise fraud or financial stress.

items.title: Fed Chairman Warsh Seeks to Calm Elevated Inflation Concerns
items.summary: In a high-profile speech, Kevin M. Warsh said the Federal Reserve was chiefly responsible for taming inflation. If price increases do not return to the central bank’s target quickly, “we have work to do,” he said.

items.title: FAFSA Form for College Aid Will Be Less Stressful This Year, Officials Say
items.summary: The college financial aid form has long been a stressor for high school seniors and their parents. Fixes have made it simpler and faster to complete, officials say.

items.title: What if the A.I. Stock Market Rally Is Just Getting Started?
items.summary: Edward Yardeni, an upbeat strategist with an excellent track record in assessing the stock market, explains why he thinks the good times will continue for years.

items.title: Warsh’s Big Test at Jackson Hole
items.summary: Investors want Kevin Warsh, the Fed chairman, to address inflation, interest rates and the bond market in a major speech. Some worry he won’t say enough.

items.title: Prediction Markets and States Clashed, Setting Off a Furious Political Battle
items.summary: A legal dispute over the future of Kalshi, Polymarket and others has drawn in the Trump administration, the president’s son and nearly every state attorney general.

items.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
items.summary: The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
items.summary: Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.

items.title: Nvidia’s Profit Doubles to $59.69 Billion Thanks to A.I. Spending
items.summary: Quarterly revenue also more than doubled, to $96.22 billion, the company said, topping expectations on Wall Street.

items.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
items.summary: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

items.title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
items.summary: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.

items.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
items.summary: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.

items.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
items.summary: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.

items.title: What Meta’s $17 Billion Settlement Means
items.summary: Our reporter Cecilia Kang explains Meta’s settlement of a lawsuit claiming that the company’s social media platforms had harmed teenage users.

items.title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
items.summary: In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.
